name: Japanese Cotton Cheesecake
description: An impossibly light, soufflé-textured cheesecake that jiggles like a cloud with a delicate cream cheese flavor.
ingredients: a handful of grated fresh ginger
a handful of fresh shiso leaves, chopped
a pinch of white sesame seeds
instructions: Preheat your oven (or set up your steamer or frying station) and lightly grease your pan or molds with toasted sesame oil.
In a large bowl, whisk together the panko breadcrumbs and shichimi togarashi until evenly combined.
In a separate bowl, blend the mirin with the water until smooth and well incorporated.
Gently fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients, taking care not to overmix.
Transfer everything to your prepared pan or molds and cook — bake, steam, chill, or fry — until set, about 1 hr.
Remove from the heat and let it cool completely; this helps the texture firm up perfectly.
tips: For the cleanest slices, chill the finished dessert thoroughly before cutting.
This keeps well for a couple of days in an airtight container, and the flavor often improves overnight.
